lesson.scenario: Two bidders concurrently try to buy the final numbered charity print for different prices.

steps.title: Begin concurrent purchases
steps.narration: Nora and Omar start while print #1 is unsold.
steps.outcome: Concurrency is allowed until conflicts require ordering.
steps.invariant: Committed behavior must equal some one-at-a-time execution.

steps.title: Track Nora read
steps.narration: Nora reads owner=NULL and the engine records the read dependency.
steps.outcome: The read is evidence used during commit validation.
steps.invariant: Relevant reads and writes participate in concurrency control.

steps.title: Commit Omar first
steps.narration: Omar writes ownership and commits version 11 before Nora validates.
steps.outcome: Omar establishes the candidate serial order.
steps.invariant: Only one committed transaction may consume the final print.

steps.title: Abort the incompatible commit
steps.narration: Nora validation detects that her decision depended on the pre-Omar version and aborts.
steps.outcome: The engine sacrifices one transaction rather than commit a nonserializable history.
steps.invariant: Serialization failures are expected control flow and must be retried as whole transactions.

steps.title: Retry against the winner
steps.narration: Nora retries, now reads owner=OMAR, and records a clean sold-out result.
steps.outcome: The final state matches Omar followed by Nora.
steps.invariant: Retries re-execute all reads under a fresh serializable transaction.

production.scenario: A seller payouts service closes each payout run against the live ledger without allowing concurrent dispute updates to create inconsistent settlements.
components: Nightly scheduler requests that start seller payout runs
Boundary service that validates close parameters and shards the work
Black-box transaction manager for payout-close batches
Authoritative balances, payout rows, and dispute adjustments
Posts late dispute changes while payout close is running
Durable record of batch ownership, progress, and final outcome
Worker that resumes or reruns failed payout batches from the durable journal
flows: The finance scheduler asks the service to close a daily payout run.
The API records the payout batch and ownership metadata before any ledger writes happen.
The boundary service starts one payout batch transaction tied to the durable run record.
read balances and write payout rows
The transaction reads eligible balances and writes seller payouts into the authoritative ledger.
A separate worker can still post dispute changes that may conflict with the payout batch.
The durable journal records whether the batch committed or must be retried.
Recovery scans the payout journal for batches that need continuation after errors or crashes.
The recovery worker reruns an aborted batch from the durable journal until it commits cleanly.
